source: To address whether hyper-activity of Aurora B/C at kinetochores could be responsible for the paucity of K-fibers in sgol2Δ/Δ oocytes, we tested the effect of the Aurora kinase inhibitor AZD1152. This both increased the density of K-fibers and reduced kinetochore stretching but did not eliminate lateral attachments (Figure 8B), which may require direct involvement of MCAK.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 8B.

claim: Sgol2 promotes chromosome bi-orientation by inhibiting Aurora B/C kinase as well as by recruiting MCAK.
source: We suggest that Sgol2 promotes chromosome bi-orientation by inhibiting Aurora B/C kinase as well as by recruiting MCAK.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the observation that Sgol2 both inhibits Aurora B/C and recruits MCAK.

claim: Sgol2 defective in PP2A binding fails to protect centromeric cohesin, as found for Sgo1 in yeast.
source: We show here that Sgol2 defective in PP2A binding fails to protect centromeric cohesin, as found for Sgo1 in yeast (Xu et al., 2009).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section and supported by a citation to Xu et al., 2009.

claim: Sgol2 deficiency caused striking changes in chromosome and microtubule dynamics during meiosis I.
source: However, if this were the sole function of Sgol2, then chromosome behavior during meiosis I should be unaffected. To our surprise, we found that Sgol2 deficiency caused striking changes in chromosome and microtubule dynamics.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section.

claim: Sgol2 deficiency delayed bi-orientation of bivalents on meiosis I spindles.
source: It delayed bi-orientation of bivalents on meiosis I spindles, caused increased bivalent stretching, and greatly increased Aurora B/C kinase activity at kinetochores, which was accompanied by an increase in lateral and a decrease in end on kinetochore-microtubules attachments.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section.

claim: Sgol2 deficiency caused increased bivalent stretching.
source: It delayed bi-orientation of bivalents on meiosis I spindles, caused increased bivalent stretching, and greatly increased Aurora B/C kinase activity at kinetochores, which was accompanied by an increase in lateral and a decrease in end on kinetochore-microtubules attachments.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section.

claim: Sgol2 deficiency greatly increased Aurora B/C kinase activity at kinetochores.
source: It delayed bi-orientation of bivalents on meiosis I spindles, caused increased bivalent stretching, and greatly increased Aurora B/C kinase activity at kinetochores, which was accompanied by an increase in lateral and a decrease in end on kinetochore-microtubules attachments.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section.

claim: Sgol2 deficiency was accompanied by an increase in lateral and a decrease in end on kinetochore-microtubules attachments.
source: It delayed bi-orientation of bivalents on meiosis I spindles, caused increased bivalent stretching, and greatly increased Aurora B/C kinase activity at kinetochores, which was accompanied by an increase in lateral and a decrease in end on kinetochore-microtubules attachments.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section.

claim: Sgol2 deficiency delayed considerably APC/CCdc20 activation.
source: Lastly, Sgol2 deficiency delayed considerably APC/CCdc20 activation, suggesting that it was required to shut off the SAC.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section.

claim: Sgol2 helps to turn off the SAC by binding directly both PP2A and the MCC protein Mad2.
source: Sgol2 helps to turn off the SAC by binding directly both PP2A and the MCC protein Mad2, it moderates chromosome stretching by recruiting to kinetochores the kinesin MCAK, and likely promotes formation of K-fibers by down-regulating the activity of Aurora B/C kinase specifically at kinetochores.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section.

claim: Sgol2 moderates chromosome stretching by recruiting to kinetochores the kinesin MCAK.
source: Sgol2 helps to turn off the SAC by binding directly both PP2A and the MCC protein Mad2, it moderates chromosome stretching by recruiting to kinetochores the kinesin MCAK, and likely promotes formation of K-fibers by down-regulating the activity of Aurora B/C kinase specifically at kinetochores.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section.

claim: Sgol2 likely promotes formation of K-fibers by down-regulating the activity of Aurora B/C kinase specifically at kinetochores.

evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section.

claim: Through its multi-domain structure, Sgol2 has an important if not unique role in coordinating many of the key processes essential for faithful chromosome segregation.
source: Our findings imply that through its multi-domain structure, Sgol2 has an important if not unique role in coordinating many of the key processes within this array.
evidence: This is a conclusion stated in the Discussion section.

claim: PP2A might protect cohesin from separase either directly, by binding and inhibiting separase activity, or indirectly, by reversing phosphorylation of cohesin's Rec8 subunit.
source: PP2A might protect cohesin from separase either directly, by binding (Holland et al., 2007) and inhibiting separase activity, or indirectly, by reversing phosphorylation of cohesin's Rec8 subunit (Katis et al., 2010), a process known to be important for its cleavage in yeast.
evidence: This is a speculation stated in the Discussion section and supported by citations to Holland et al., 2007 and Katis et al., 2010.

claim: Sgol2 silences the SAC by competing with Cdc20 for the binding of activated Mad2, thereby preventing formation of the MCC.
source: This raises the possibility that Sgol2 silences the SAC by competing with Cdc20 for the binding of activated Mad2, thereby preventing formation of the MCC.
evidence: This is a speculation stated in the Discussion section.

claim: PP2A directly (i.e., structurally) facilitates the formation or stability of 'closed' complexes between Sgol2 and Mad2.
source: Because Sgol2's MIM motif is close to the coiled coil by which it binds PP2A, it is conceivable that PP2A directly (i.e., structurally) facilitates the formation or stability of 'closed' complexes between Sgol2 and Mad2.
evidence: This is a speculation stated in the Discussion section.

claim: Only dephosphorylated Mad2 interacts with Cdc20 and Sgol2, while a phosphomimetic mutant of Mad2 cannot associate with either of these proteins.
source: This hypothesis is supported by the fact that only dephosphorylated Mad2 interacts with Cdc20 and Sgol2, while a phosphomimetic mutant of Mad2 cannot associate with either of these proteins (personal communication Michael Orth).
evidence: This is supported by a personal communication from Michael Orth.

claim: PP2A could selectively stabilize the Sgol2: Mad2 complex formation by keeping Mad2 in a de-phosphorylated state.
source: Thus, PP2A could selectively stabilize the Sgol2-Mad2 complex by keeping Mad2 in a de-phosphorylated state.
evidence: This is a speculation stated in the Discussion section.

claim: If there were sufficient turnover of Mad2 bound to MCC, then PP2A could promote the Sgol2: Mad2 complex formation and thus alter the activity of the MCC responsible for inhibiting the APC/C.
source: Therefore, it is conceivable that if there were sufficient turnover of Mad2 bound to MCC, then PP2A could promote the Sgol2: Mad2 complex formation and thus alter the activity of the MCC responsible for inhibiting the APC/C.
evidence: This is a speculation stated in the Discussion section.

claim: It is the population of MCAK recruited to kinetochores by Sgol2 that moderates the pulling forces exerted on maternal and paternal kinetochores, possibly by reducing the incidence of lateral attachments.
source: Because artificial recruitment of MCAK to kinetochores by fusion to CENP-B substitutes for Sgol2 with regard to bivalent stretching, we suggest that it is the population of MCAK recruited to kinetochores by Sgol2 that moderates the pulling forces exerted on maternal and paternal kinetochores, possibly by reducing the incidence of lateral attachments.
evidence: This is a conclusion stated in the Discussion section.

claim: xSgo2, a newly discovered homolog of shugoshin in Xenopus, promotes Aurora Kinase activity, generating a favourable environment for microtubule polymerization.
source: The notion that Sgol2 moderates Aurora B/C kinase activity at kinetochores was unexpected, as it has been reported that xSgo2, a newly discovered homolog of shugoshin in Xenopus, actually promotes Aurora Kinase activity, generating a favourable environment for microtubule polymerization (Rivera et al., 2012).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Rivera et al., 2012.

claim: xSgo2's effect on Aurora Kinase activity may be systemic, that is throughout the cytoplasm, whereas M.m Sgol2 appears to act as an inhibitor only at kinetochores.
source: In this case, the effect may be systemic, that is throughout the cytoplasm, whereas M.m Sgol2 appears to act as an inhibitor only at kinetochores.
evidence: This is a speculation stated in the Discussion section.

claim: It has been assumed that the mechanism responsible for turning off Aurora B/C kinases merely involved physical forces that pull Aurora substrates away from the enzymes when maternal and paternal kinetochores are pulled in opposite directions.
source: Hitherto, it has been assumed that the mechanism responsible for turning off these kinases merely involved physical forces that pull Aurora substrates away from the enzymes when maternal and paternal kinetochores are pulled in opposite directions (Liu et al., 2009).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Liu et al., 2009.

claim: Down regulation of Aurora B/C is also an intrinsic feature of a biochemical system in which Aurora B/C activates its own inhibitor.
source: Though our work does not preclude a role for traction in down regulating Aurora B/C's access to kinetochore-bound substrates, it raises the possibility that down regulation is also an intrinsic feature of a biochemical system in which Aurora B/C activates its own inhibitor.
evidence: This is a conclusion stated in the Discussion section.

claim: The regulatory network revealed by this work ensures that Aurora B/C kinases will be active early during the bi-orientation, when incorrect attachments may be more frequent, and less active later, when they have been largely eliminated.
source: The regulatory network revealed by our work ensures that Aurora B/C kinases will be active early during the bi-orientation, when incorrect attachments may be more frequent, and less active later, when they have been largely eliminated.
evidence: This is a conclusion stated in the Discussion section.

claim: During the period when Aurora B/C kinases are active, the selective stabilization of correct attachments is mediated by mechanical changes within kinetochores induced by tension, as recently observed in purified yeast kinetochores.
source: It is possible that during the period when Aurora B/C kinases are active, the selective stabilization of correct attachments is mediated by mechanical changes within kinetochores induced by tension, as recently observed in purified yeast kinetochores (Akiyoshi et al., 2010), not as originally thought by tension dependent changes in Aurora kinase activity, for which there has never been much direct evidence.
evidence: This is a speculation stated in the Discussion section and supported by a citation to Akiyoshi et al., 2010.

claim: An important feature of meiosis I in oocytes is an early phase of high Aurora B/C kinase activity at kinetochores followed by a later phase of lowered activity made possible by the Aurora B/C-Sgol2 negative feedback loop.
source: We suggest that an important feature of meiosis I in oocytes is an early phase of high Aurora B/C kinase activity at kinetochores followed by a later phase of lowered activity made possible by the Aurora B/C-Sgol2 negative feedback loop.
evidence: This is a conclusion stated in the Discussion section.

claim: The lowered activity of Aurora B/C might increase the MT-depolymerizing activity of MCAK at kinetochores.
source: The lowered activity of Aurora B/C might increase the MT-depolymerizing activity of MCAK at kinetochores (Andrews et al., 2004).
evidence: This is a speculation stated in the Discussion section and supported by a citation to Andrews et al., 2004.

claim: The kinetochore pool of MCAK, recruited by Sgol2, is not phosphorylated at serine 92 in mouse oocytes.
source: This is supported by the fact that the kinetochore pool of MCAK, recruited by Sgol2, is indeed not phosphorylated at serine 92 in mouse oocytes (data not shown).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section.

claim: sgol2Δ/Δ oocytes often manage to undergo the first meiotic division without generating massive aneuploidy.
source: Given the number of fundamental processes regulated by Sgol2, it is surprising that sgol2Δ/Δ oocytes often manage to undergo the first meiotic division without generating massive aneuploidy.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section.

claim: The second meiotic division of sgol2Δ/Δ oocytes is completely defective due to the total absence of sister chromatid cohesion.
source: Their second meiotic division is of course completely defective due to the total absence of sister chromatid cohesion.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section.

claim: All of the processes regulated by Sgol2 are fundamentally essential but they are also regulated by Sgol2-independent pathways.
source: We suggest that all of the processes regulated by Sgol2 are fundamentally essential but that they are also regulated by Sgol2-independent pathways.
evidence: This is a speculation stated in the Discussion section.

claim: Sgol1, which is also expressed during meiosis, may share some functions with Sgol2.
source: It is not inconceivable that Sgol1, which is also expressed during meiosis, shares some functions with Sgol2 and it will therefore be interesting to analyze the phenotype of double mutant oocytes.
evidence: This is a speculation stated in the Discussion section.

claim: A single protein (Sgol2) regulates sister chromatid cohesion, chromosome traction, the spindle assembly checkpoint, and Aurora B/C kinases.
source: What is possibly most remarkable is that a single protein regulates sister chromatid cohesion, chromosome traction, the spindle assembly checkpoint, and lastly Aurora B/C kinases.
evidence: This is a conclusion stated in the Discussion section.

claim: Different point mutations in Sgol2 alter the regulation of some but not other processes, proving that the pleiotropy observed in sgol2Δ/Δ oocytes is not due to knock on effects.
source: Crucially, by demonstrating that different point mutations alter the regulation of some but not other processes, we have proven that the pleiotropy observed in sgol2Δ/Δ oocytes is not due to knock on effects (secondary or even tertiary pathology) of eliminating a single function.
evidence: This is a conclusion stated in the Discussion section.

claim: Sgol2 possesses several different domains that regulate fundamentally different processes.
source: Sgol2 possesses several different domains that regulate fundamentally different processes (Figure 11).
evidence: This is a conclusion stated in the Discussion section and shown in Figure 11.

claim: The embedding of so much regulation into a single protein (Sgol2) helps the coordination of multiple processes necessary for high fidelity chromosome segregation.
source: Why so much regulation is embedded into a single protein is unclear, but we speculate that this helps the coordination of multiple processes necessary for high fidelity chromosome segregation.
evidence: This is a speculation stated in the Discussion section.
